To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social control of social research is exercised through the gatekeepers who are located within the research institutions, that the gatekeepers have the capacity to limit the conditions under which research can be conducted, and that researchers must create autonomous bases of support in order to conduct research that is critical of powerful institutions.

the gatekeepers' control of research is exercised in the areas of: (1) the definition of the research problem; (2) the control of data; (3) the control of respondents; and (4) the control of publication of the research.

gatekeeping is the social control of the social sciences, that gatekeepers are found in all social science research settings, that the gatekeeping role is not well understood by the social scientist, and that the social scientist is often unaware that he is being gatekept.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) how the gatekeeper influences the research endeavor; (2) the nature of the gatekeeping relationship; and (3) the implications of the gatekeeper for the research process.
the ways in which the gatekeepers of the social research community control the research endeavor. (Author/JM)
the nature of gatekeeping in social research, the social control of social research, and the development of strategies for dealing with the social control of the research process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social control of social research has become an important and growing problem.

gatekeeping is an integral and pervasive part of the research enterprise, that it has the capacity for influencing the direction of the research, and that it is a problem for researchers and their institutions to manage.
the "gatekeeper" phenomenon, in the form of institutionalized social control of research, is a serious problem for the social scientist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found the gatekeepers to be the key figures in the process of social control of social research.
gatekeeping is a major problem for social research, and it is a problem which is not likely to disappear in the near future.
the gatekeeper is a social agent of control, but that the social agent of control can be controlled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social control of social research is a serious problem.
researchers must be willing to challenge the status quo and to question the assumptions that underlie the social control of their work.
gatekeepers are not always the most obvious people in a research setting, but they are often powerful and influential.
